review_text: Spotify is amazing. It enables me to access the music I enjoy listening to and to create a number of playlists with different music styles, specific artists, artists, etc and only including those songs and tunes I want on the playlist. Of the playlists I have made public, one currently has been saved by 3,400 people and another 270. It is encouraging to know others are enjoying a playlist when this happens. The shuffle aspect is a great feature so the order can randomly change. I have given my CD collection to charity shops since subscribing. I also enjoy accessing nonfiction podcasts and free audiobooks. It can be a bit frustrating when an audiobook is withdrawn if I want to listen again. The ability to access and save podcasts is also useful and to replay them at my leisure. The sleep timer is very clever as I regularly listen to podcasts at night as they enable me to eventually drift off to sleep. Podcasts are both educational and stimulating. Thank you, Spotify.

title: Protect your mental health by avoiding this harmful, addictive app.
review_text: It might feel good in the moment, but our brains are not built to constantly receive pleasure this easily. Every time you see a new video, dopamine is released. Now imagine seeing 500 videos in under 30 minutes. Imagine what that does to your brain. Ever wondered why the things you used to love no longer interest you? Why you dont watch movies anymore? Why you cant focus on anything? Its because brains adapt. Our brains adapt to the constant influx of pleasure by increasing the “baseline”. This baseline means that things that once made you feel good dont give the same effect, because it doesn’t compare at all to the dopamine (happy hormone) that you get in the same span of time. So you end up neglecting the things that really matter. Real dopamine. Please, protect your mental health and don’t download this. If you already have, delete it. And never get it back.

title: Disabled my account
review_text:
I wish I could give Instagram 5 stars because it has always been my favourite social media app. Unfortunately, I recently had my account permanently disabled after being accused of violating one of Meta’s most serious policies—something I strongly believe I did not do.

To the best of my knowledge, I followed Instagram’s Community Standards and did not intentionally violate any of its rules.

I completed every step Instagram asked of me, including the appeal process, video selfie verification, and ID verification. Despite this, my account was permanently disabled. I was never told which specific photo, message, or activity allegedly violated the policy, making it impossible to understand or challenge the decision.

To make matters worse, I can’t even download my own information because the feature repeatedly says “Something went wrong.” I have also found it extremely difficult to contact a real person, as almost every support route redirects me back to my disabled account.

Losing memories, conversations, and connections has been devastating. I understand that Instagram must enforce its Community Standards, but there should also be a fair and transparent process when mistakes happen. I sincerely hope Meta improves its review system and provides users with meaningful human support when accounts are permanently disabled.

title: Privacy breach- Very very unsafe platform (instagram does not help to protect your privacy)
review_text:
I am very disappointed with Instagram’s account recovery and security support. My account was hacked, and despite still having access to the associated email and receiving login codes, the recovery process does not restore access properly.
The system keeps looping through verification steps without allowing full account recovery, even though unauthorized login attempts are clearly being detected (for example, login alerts from unknown devices).
This creates a serious security concern. A user can still receive verification emails but remain locked out of their own account, while the attacker may still maintain control or re-establish access.
Instagram’s current recovery flow is confusing, inconsistent, and not effective in helping legitimate users regain access to compromised accounts.
I strongly urge Instagram to improve:
Clearer recovery steps when email access is still valid
A direct way to override unauthorized sessions after verification
Faster human support for hacked accounts
Better protection against account takeover persistence
Account security should not depend on repeated failed loops or unclear verification paths. This experience has been frustrating and does not inspire confidence in Instagram’s ability to protect users.

The YouTube algorithm is just so, so ineffective.

title: Ads, Bugs, A.i, Reels
review_text:
Ads are constantly forced down my throat. I can’t properly block them, and they continue playing anyway. There are disturbing ads for AI romance bots, and even if I block one, a new company shows up the next day. On top of that, there’s AI slop everywhere. Forget personal YouTube videos voiced by actual humans. YouTube is becoming SlopTube.
Reels are forced down your throat on homepage. They’ve limited the amount of actual videos on my homepage while pushing more reels instead. This makes things worse for creators because there are fewer video slots available, while more money and attention are being directed toward reels. The algorithm has progressively gotten worse.
I have every privacy and data setting turned OFF. I am not logged into YouTube on my TV. Yet videos and suggestions related to my personal account still show up on my family TV. Google and YouTube privacy settings are all OFF. The TV is only in Guest Mode. That’s disturbing and invasive.
At least once a week, YouTube asks if I want to watch on my lounge room TV while I’m outside in my garage. Or anywhere else. No. I don’t even want you knowing I have that TV in my lounge room. I’ve turned all privacy settings off, yet you keep asking if I want to switch devices without any prompt from me.
Stop scanning my local Wi-Fi when I don’t want to log in, use that TV, or have that functionality active in the first place.
Then there’s the homepage. I’ll scroll through it and see 10–20 written or image posts mixed in, like YouTube is trying to become Twitter or Instagram. I wouldn’t care if it was one or two every now and then, but not to the extent it is now.
The skip button often doesn’t work unless the video is minimised into a small screen, or sometimes it doesn’t work at all. Ads are forced on you and can’t be skipped. Sometimes the app locks itself in fullscreen during ads, and even rotating the phone won’t let you get out of it.
The ad experience is terrible. You can’t listen to music comfortably because some stupid, loud, infuriating ad suddenly blasts through your speakers and ruins everything. You’re constantly having to adjust the volume because ad volume and content volume aren’t balanced. Or is some infuriating brain rot slop ads over and over. Even if you block an ad THEY WILL SHOW IT AGAIN. 
This app has gotten progressively worse and worse.
Let me block ads. Don’t force me to watch things I don’t want to see. Stop forcing more ads when YouTube already makes more than enough money.
YouTube was meant to be about us. Instead, it’s become CorporateTube, where you’re treated as a number for algorithms, engagement metrics, and data collection. That’s exactly what it feels like now. You’re only seen as a dollar sign.
People can blame creators if they want, but the ability for all of this to happen and how creators handle it exists because YouTube allows it on their platform. The ball is in YouTube’s court. But they’re too busy looking probably at A.i or more stupid quick feeding entertainment and engagement, I won’t be surprised if they add watch streaks of some sort next to try make people feel forced to come on. Don’t recommend even though there isn’t another option. It’s a terrible monopoly.
